summary: The @gyomu/approval-core package provides the foundational domain models, interfaces, and service definitions for managing complex approval workflows. It establishes a standardized architecture for tracking request lifecycles, evaluating policy-based decisions, and maintaining immutable audit histories for both automated and manual interventions.
responsibilities: Define domain-driven data structures for approval requests, statuses, and evaluation decisions.
Establish architectural contracts (ports) for initiating approval requests and managing request state persistence.
Standardize input schemas for lifecycle operations such as approving or rejecting requests.
Provide service interfaces for querying historical approval records across users and tools.
Ensure consistent traceability and data integrity throughout the approval workflow lifecycle.

capabilities.name: Approval Workflow Modeling
capabilities.description: Defines the core lifecycle, statuses, and challenge structures necessary to represent complex approval requests within the system.

capabilities.name: Policy Evaluation Results
capabilities.description: Standardizes the outcome of approval policy checks, allowing for clear distinction between approved, denied, or pending decisions.

capabilities.name: Lifecycle Management Ports
capabilities.description: Provides abstract interfaces for submitting new requests and managing their state, enabling decoupling from infrastructure implementations.

capabilities.name: Audit and History Tracking
capabilities.description: Enables retrieval of historical approval events, facilitating auditability and data analysis for users and integrated tools.

designDecisions: Utilizes a port-and-adapter architectural pattern to decouple domain logic from specific persistence or submission mechanisms.
Implements strong typing for lifecycle commands to ensure consistency and prevent invalid state transitions.
Aggregates core domain logic into a unified surface area to simplify integration for consuming modules.
Focuses on functional definitions to allow for integration with both manual user interactions and automated policy engines.
usageGuidance: Implement the provided port interfaces when integrating with your specific storage or transport layers.
Use the defined command input types to ensure consistency when building UI or API controllers that trigger approval workflows.
Reference the domain models when extending policy evaluation logic to ensure alignment with existing status and decision types.
Leverage the history service interface to build reporting or audit logging capabilities for your application.
